Also notes increased mujahidin recruitment since the Chechnya conflict resumed in 1999, with training at al-Qa'ida camps in Afghanistan.

events.description: CIA Senior Executive Intelligence Brief reports a surge in Sunni terrorist plotting linked to Bin Ladin's network.
Resumption of conflict in Chechnya triggers a sharp increase in mujahidin recruitment and training at al-Qa'ida camps in Afghanistan.
Bombing of the USS Cole; suspects first tried to attack a US warship in Aden; Yemeni and Saudi jihadists with varying ties to Bin Ladin implicated.

key_claims: An energized international jihad movement is raising the threat to US interests, especially in the Middle East and Europe.
Bin Ladin remains the most influential figure in the movement.
The newly detected plots are the biggest spike in network terrorist activity since the millennium.
Bin Ladin has let al-Qa'ida cells plan more independently to avoid implicating himself and his Taliban hosts.
Mujahidin recruitment surged after the 1999 resumption of the Chechnya conflict, with training at al-Qa'ida camps in Afghanistan.
The USS Cole investigation points to Yemeni and Saudi jihadists with varying ties to Bin Ladin.
